question.text: In case of nitrogen, <math><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> is possible but not <math><mi>N</mi><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> while in case of phosphorous, <math><mi>P</mi><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> as well as <math><mi>P</mi><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> are possible. It is due to

options.text: Availability of vacant d orbitals in <math> <mtext>P</mtext> </math> but not in <math> <mtext>N</mtext> </math>
Lower tendency of H-bond formation in <math> <mtext>P</mtext></math> than <math> <mtext>N</mtext></math>
Occurrence of <math> <mtext>P</mtext></math> in solid while <math> <mtext>N</mtext></math> in gaseous state at room temperature.

solution.text:
N7=1s22s22p3; P15=1s22s22p63s23p3

In phosphorous the 3d-orbitals are available. Hence phosphorus can form pentahalides also but nitrogen cannot form pentahalide due to absence of d-orbitals.
